title: Arrange a row with flex
summary: React Native uses Flexbox for layout. Its default direction is a column, so set row when items should sit beside each other.
introduction: React Native uses Flexbox for layout. Its default direction is a column, so set row when items should sit beside each other. Your task: Change row to column and compare the layout.
learningObjectives: Change row to column and compare the layout.

blocks.text: React Native uses Flexbox for layout. Its default direction is a column, so set row when items should sit beside each other.

blocks.code:
import {View,Text} from "react-native";
export default function App(){return <View style={{padding:24,flexDirection:"row",gap:12}}><Text>Books read</Text><Text>4</Text></View>;}
blocks.title: Arrange a row with flex

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `flexDirection` chooses the main layout direction. React Native uses `column` by default; `row` places children beside each other.

blocks.text: The label and count appear side by side with a gap.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Do not assume the default direction matches browser CSS flex rows. Native defaults to column.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Change row to column and compare the layout.
